reverse engineered UML class diagram representations can be used to verify Java implementation code, that the differences between forward and reverse engineered representations can be automatically identified and reported, and that these differences can be used to guide human inspection of the implementation.

the verification of Java implementations using reverse engineering.
the development of a tool that automatically verifies that an implementation is consistent to the original design.
the use of reverse engineering to verify Java code against its original design, and the use of automated comparison to guide the code inspection process.

the automated comparison of forward engineered and reverse engineered artefacts provides an additional tool to help software engineers identify potential errors in the final implementation.
the automated verification of forward engineering is feasible but not without challenges.
the reverse engineering process is not a replacement for code inspection, but it can be used to augment the process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of automated tools to compare forward engineered and reverse engineered design artefacts is a valuable addition to the software development process.
the use of reverse engineering to support verification is feasible.
